title: a vendored warning's example URI, postgresql://user:\$$v@host, reads as a credential to a secret scanner, so every estate that scans its tree has to baseline a line of devbin's
body:
## Problem

`generated_doc_write`'s refusal when a denied variable's value appears in a generated block (lib/helpers:2798) advises env indirection with an example connection URI: `Use env indirection in the producer's output (postgresql://user:\$$v@host) rather than the value.` The line is vendored, so it sits at `bin/.devbin/lib/helpers` in every estate, and a secret scanner reads `postgresql://user:\$$v@host` as a Postgres connection string carrying a password.

Reported on 2026-10-07 by another estate's session: its secret-scan gate, Kingfisher 2.11.0, flagged the line in a repository carrying devbin 0.1.9, and it was the one false positive in that repository's whole history. Every estate that scans its tree has to baseline a line of devbin's, and a baseline that excuses a credential-shaped string is an exemption that can later hide a real one. The printed warning carries the same shape, `postgresql://user:$PGPASSWORD@host`, into whatever log captures it.

## Measured (vc, 2026-10-08, main 4f3d5601)

- `git grep -nE '[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://[^/[:space:]]*@' -- lib bin` finds one line in the whole vendored set: lib/helpers:2798. cc found the same line independently.
- No arm asserts the refusal's advice: gendoc.bats's R1 arm asserts only that the refusal names `PGPASSWORD`.
- The same shape is in devbin's own tree outside the vendored set: docs/authoring-commands.md:444 recommends `postgresql://user:$PGPASSWORD@host/db`, and gendoc.bats's R1 arms plant `postgresql://u:s3cr3t-value@host/db` as the leak and `postgresql://u:$PGPASSWORD@host/db` as the safe form. Neither reaches a consumer, so neither is this issue's.
- Kingfisher is not installed on this machine. Homebrew carries kingfisher 2.11.0, the reported version.

## Fix

The refusal keeps its advice, env indirection, without a URI carrying a password: eg "Use env indirection in the producer's output -- write \$$v where the value would go -- rather than the value." A shape arm in tests/unit/neutral.bats, beside the arms that hold commits and machine paths, refuses a URI carrying a password (`scheme://user:password@`, the env-indirection form included, since a scanner cannot tell the two apart) in any file `vendored_paths` lists, with planted positives and negatives like its neighbours'.

## Done when

1. The refusal still names the variable and still advises env indirection, and the R1 arm asserts the advice, so a rewording that drops it is red.
2. The neutral.bats arm is red on main first, naming lib/helpers:2798, and green with the fix; its planted negatives hold a URI with a user and no password (`ssh://git@host/x`), a plain URL and an email address as innocent.
3. Kingfisher 2.11.0 finds the line in the vendored set on main and nothing there with the fix, driven on this machine; if it cannot be installed here, the Resolution says so rather than claiming the scanner's verdict.

## Resolution

Landed at 6490f18f on a green full suite (vc's, 2257 of 2257 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261008-0811).

- **The refusal (Done when 1).** generated_doc_write's refusal keeps its advice and names the variable, with no example URI: "Use env indirection in the producer's output -- write the literal text $<VAR> where the value would go -- rather than the value." R1's refusal arm asserts that advice and refutes both "://" and the refused value in what the refusal prints. A rewording that drops the advice, brings a URI back or prints the value is therefore red.
- **The neutral.bats arm (Done when 2).** A credentials arm refuses a URI carrying a password, `scheme://user:password@`, an env indirection included, in any file vendored_paths lists. It reads the user and password as RFC 3986 reads userinfo, with eight planted positives and eleven planted negatives, among them `ssh://git@host/x`, a plain URL and an email address. It is red on main 674a7608, before batch 3, naming lib/helpers:2798, and red on 0186 v1.1, which it is built on, naming the same line at :2937. It is green with the fix.
- **Kingfisher (Done when 3).** Kingfisher 2.11.0, from its GitHub release and checked against the digest GitHub publishes, was driven on this machine. It finds the line on main before batch 3 (9f21eb3d), betterleaks.generic-credential-uri at lib/helpers:2798, and at :2937 on 0186 v1.1. With the fix it finds nothing in the 74-file vendored set, at the default confidence and at low. Homebrew's 2.11.1 answers the same.

Thirteen mutants, thirteen killed.

docs/authoring-commands.md:444 and gendoc.bats's R1 fixtures carry the same shape outside the vendored set and are not this issue's.
